topics.topic: AuditEntry sequence identity and number reuse after backup restore
questions: After restoring a backup, is this the same store, requiring the sequence to continue above every number written before the restore, or a new store incarnation allowed to reuse numbers lost by the restore?

After restoring a backup whose last sequence is N, when the same store had previously written later entries, does the next entry reuse N+1, preserve the pre-restore high-water mark, or belong to a new store identity against which sequence numbers are scoped?
After restoring an older backup, may Registry mint sequence numbers that the same store had already assigned to post-backup entries, or must it preserve a high-water mark that prevents their reuse?

quotes:
its sequence number, minted by Registry: 1 for the store's first entry, then
  one more than the last its store ever wrote; never reused in that store,
  also after old entries are erased (R0-66), so the log's order is the order
  of the numbers even where two entries share an instant (owner, 2026-10-31;
  codex round-02 T2).
judgement.why: Continuing from an older backup's last number reuses numbers already written after that backup, contrary to the assertion that numbers are never reused in that store.

topics.topic: Action that validates the MigrationClosure backup and triggers deletion of pre-import backups
questions: What product or administrative action checks a backup containing the MigrationClosure, and does successful completion of that action trigger deletion of every pre-import backup?

topics.topic: Whether backup restore may remove AuditEntries outside the audit-erasure lifecycle
questions: Does restoring a backup legitimately remove AuditEntries without the dated audit-erasure action and without recording an erasure entry, and if so is backup loss part of the AuditEntry lifecycle?
